d.t: WHEREAS: 1. The City of Vancouver is the owner of all the streets and lanes lying within the limits of the City of Vancouver; 2. There is a proposal to construct a new daycare facility to be leased to the Young Men’s Christian Association (the “YMCA”), onto a portion of lane adjacent to PID: 007-044-054, Lot E, Block 159, District Lot 264A, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 19383, Except: Part Shown on Plan BCP31198; 3. The said portion of lane, more particularly described as PID: 027-132-153, That Portion Lot E Shown on Plan BCP31198, Block 159, District Lot 264A, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 19383 established as lane by document BB275975 deposited in the New Westminster Land Title Office on July 12, 2007 and by resolution passed by Council on July 10, 2007; 4. The proposal requires that the said portion of lane to be occupied by the new facility be closed, stopped-up and leased to the YMCA; and 5. The said portion of lane is no longer required for municipal purposes. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT all that portion of lane, adjacent to PID: 007-044- 054, Lot E, Block 159, District Lot 264A, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 19383, Except: Part Shown on Plan BCP31198, and more particularly described as PID: 027-132-153 That Portion Lot E Shown on Plan BCP31198, Block 159, District Lot 264A, Group 1, New Westminster District, Plan 19383 be closed, stopped-up and leased to the YMCA.
d.pl: Lane portion closed and leased to the YMCA for a new daycare

d.t: THAT the application of the Strathcona Area Merchants Association, with the exclusion of 611 Alexander Street and the properties on the north side of 1300 Block Powell Street, be approved and that the Director of Legal Services, in consultation with the Director of City Plans, prepare a by-law to establish the BIA and funding ceiling, subject to: i. THAT approval of the proposed BIA be conditional on the Strathcona Area Merchants Society agreeing to participate in and abide by the outcome of facilitated, and if necessary mediated, discussions through the Downtown Eastside Community Revitalization Program, with affected community groups, to resolve issues that may arise from any initiatives which may affect conditions on the street, including reducing the negative impacts of the illegal drug trade and street prostitution. ii. THAT, as a condition of approval of funding, the Strathcona BIA agree in principle to reimburse non-profit societies the share of the BIA levy paid to their landlord. The detailed mechanism for reimbursement will be developed by the BIA and staff, in consultation with the community.
d.pl: Strathcona business improvement area approved, tied to community talks
